newsitem.title: UK: EMS/Mark bounces off lows vs French franc, lira.
newsitem.headline: EMS/Mark bounces off lows vs French franc, lira.

text.p: 1335 GMT - Mark edges up vs French franc and lira after dipping close to session lows, dismisses EMU-related comments from top European officials at Global 24 forex conference.
* Germany's Kohl says confident Bonn will meet "three-point-zero" EMU deficit target in 1997 and 1998 and launch EMU on time, German GDP of 2.5 pct in 1997 and 3.0 in 1998 possible.
* Bavarian premier Stoiber welcomes Kohl remark on targets.
* German finmin Waigel says no automatic entry for EMU, convergence more important than timetable.
* German finmin's Stark says to make proposal on converting German debt into euro by summer break, all tradeable govt paper to be converted to euro from 1999.
* Buba's Tietmeyer, Bank of France's Trichet, Dutch cenbank's Duisenberg to speak at conference later today. Buba's Jochimsen and Welteke speak later at separate events.
* Portugal finmin says has good chance of joining EMU in 1999. Mark/escudo at 100.96/98 vs 101.04/07 late Monday.
* Italy no longer needs weak lira policy tool as inflation receded, says senior Italy treasury/budget ministry official.
* Mark/Paris at 3.3704/09, edging off one-month low of 3.3696 and vs 3.3707/11 Monday. Mark/lira at 973.40/60 after falling to 5-mth low of 972.20 overnight, vs 975.40/55 Monday.
-- MIDDAY REPORT --

The mark was crawling off its session lows on the crosses at Europe's midday, its sentiment dampened by strength in the dollar and sterling, both of which rose to multi-year highs against the mark earlier.
The market was keeping an eye on comments by top-level European government and central bank officials gathered today at the Global 24 international forex conference on European monetary union.
However, traders said currencies moved very little on the comments as the officials had so far said nothing new.

"The mark's had a weak tone all morning, carrying over its mood from yesterday, but there aren't any signs that the market is reacting to today's comments in particular," said Itsuro Karasawa, assistant general manager at Sakura Bank in London.
"Basically we all know the sort of things these officials are inclined to say and they're not likely to say anything radical at this point," Karasawa said.

Traders had been keeping a lookout today following comments made over the weekend by Bavarian premier Edmund Stoiber, who insisted that EMU should be delayed if candidate members could not fulfill the criteria.
What the market got were the familiar remarks from German Chancellor Helmut Kohl that he was confident Germany would fulfill the EMU criteria and that the single currency would be launched on time.
The French franc was at 3.3703/09 per mark at 1145 GMT, edging off the one-month high of 3.3696 it reached earlier and just above the 3.3707/11 seen in late European trade on Monday.
The lira was at 973.10/40 to the mark, down from the five-month high of 972.20 overnight but above Monday's 975.40/55.

"It's been trying to push towards the (overnight mark/lira) low again, but at these levels people are a bit wary of central bank intervention so that's stopped as well," said one trader at a British bank.
"The closer we get to the end of the 2.5 percent band in the ERM, which works out to around 966 lire, the more intervention we're likely to see from the Bank of Italy," he said.

Stoiber may have added another twist to the EMU saga over the weekend but this has not changed the market's perceptions about who will be included in monetary union, since the lira had moved but not the other peripheral currencies, traders said.
Mark/peseta was at 84.51/52, unchanged from Friday, while mark/escudo was at 100.89/95 against 101.04/07.
The market was unlikely to see comments with much substance until later this month, when France's audit of public finances and Germany's budget are due to be presented, they said.

"There is a lot of speculation going around about budget deficits and so on, and the markets are likely to twitch back and forth on those. But even if (French and German) officials make comments, no-one will ever say anything definite until the actual numbers are out," Sakura's Karasawa said.
-- Chizu Nomiyama, London Forex Desk, +44-171-542-6721
